# Species, Baits, Lures & Rigs (SC, fall)

> Limits: SCDNR eRegulations 2026–27, checked 10/11/2026. [Official regs](https://www.eregulations.com/southcarolina/fishing). This guide is a reminder, not the law.
> Rigs are written for the family's three setups (see bottom).

## Quick pick: what to fish for in October–November

| With kids, easy | Best fight | Best eating (check advisories) |
|---|---|---|
| Whiting, spot, croaker (pier, 2-hook rig + shrimp) · Bluegill/bream (bobber + worm) | Bull red drum (release!) · Bluefish · Striped bass (Santee, opens Oct 1) | Flounder (16″+) · Seatrout (14″+) · Whiting · Crappie (8″+) |

## Saltwater

### Red Drum

*Also called: redfish, spottail bass, puppy drum, bull red*

- **ID:** Copper-bronze body, one or more black spots at the base of the tail, NO chin whiskers.
- **Look-alikes:** Black drum has chin barbels and no tail spot. Spot (the small fish) has a shoulder spot, not a tail spot.
- **SC limits:** 18–25" TL · 1/person/day · 2/boat. New July 1, 2026: 18–25″ slot, 1/person, 2/boat. Natural bait on hooks 4/0+ must be a non-offset, non-stainless CIRCLE hook. Nearly every fall bull red is over the slot: release it fast.
- **Oct–Nov:** Peak season. Adults leave the inlets late Oct–Nov and run the beaches ("bull red run"). Slot reds stack in creeks and along jetties on falling tides.
- **Where (kid-friendliest first):** Surfside Pier · Myrtle Beach State Park Pier · Murrells Inlet MarshWalk / Morse Park Landing · Mount Pleasant Pier · Apache Pier · Springmaid Pier
- **Bait:** Cut or live finger mullet · Cut menhaden (pogy) · Blue crab (halved) · Live shrimp
- **Lures:** Gold weedless spoon · 3–4″ paddletail on 1/4 oz jighead · Gulp! Shrimp · Topwater walker at dawn
- **Rig it:**
  - *Saltwater rod:* Fishfinder (slide) rig: 2–4 oz pyramid sinker, swivel, 24–30″ of 30–40 lb fluoro, 5/0–7/0 NON-offset, NON-stainless circle hook (required w/ natural bait), cut mullet. Rod in a holder; when it loads up, just reel.
  - *Freshwater rod:* For slot reds in creeks: 1/4 oz jighead + paddletail on 10 lb braid / 15–20 lb fluoro leader. Too light for bulls.
  - *Kids' Ugly Stik:* Slot reds only: 2-hook bottom rig with shrimp. Bulls will spool an Ugly Stik, so hand off to an adult.

### Spotted Seatrout

*Also called: speckled trout, speck, trout*

- **ID:** Silvery with round black spots on the back, the dorsal fin AND the tail; 1–2 fang-like canine teeth up front; yellow-orange mouth inside.
- **Look-alikes:** Weakfish: spots in wavy diagonal rows, no spots on fins. Silver seatrout: no spots.
- **SC limits:** 14" min TL · 10/person/day. Saltwater gamefish: circle-hook rule applies to natural bait on 4/0+ hooks. No gigging Dec 1–Feb 28.
- **Oct–Nov:** October–November is the peak. Cold fronts kick the bite on; fish move to deeper creek bends and channels as water drops below ~60°F.
- **Where (kid-friendliest first):** Murrells Inlet MarshWalk / Morse Park Landing · Mount Pleasant Pier · Georgetown: East Bay Park / Winyah Bay · Pawleys Island (surf & creek) · Garris Landing (Cape Romain NWR) · Huntington Beach SP: Murrells Inlet South Jetty
- **Bait:** Live shrimp (#1 bait by far) · Live finger mullet · Mud minnows
- **Lures:** Popping cork + Vudu/Gulp shrimp · MirrOlure suspending twitchbait · 3″ paddletail on 1/8–1/4 oz jighead · Topwater at dawn
- **Rig it:**
  - *Saltwater rod:* Popping cork: 24–30″ of 20 lb fluoro under the cork, #1–1/0 kahle or circle hook through the shrimp's horn. Pop it every 10–15 sec.
  - *Freshwater rod:* Your freshwater rod is IDEAL for trout: 10 lb braid / 15 lb fluoro, 1/8 oz jighead + soft plastic, slow-roll near the bottom.
  - *Kids' Ugly Stik:* Slip float or clip-on bobber, 18–24″ leader, #1 hook, live shrimp. Kids catch a lot of trout this way.

### Southern Flounder

*Also called: flounder, flatfish, doormat, summer flounder, gulf flounder*

- **ID:** Flat; both eyes on the LEFT side; brown with diffuse spots. SC regs treat all flounder species as one.
- **Look-alikes:** Summer flounder: 5 eye-like spots. Gulf flounder: 3 eyespots in a triangle. Same limits either way.
- **SC limits:** 16" min TL · 5/person/day · 10/boat. 16″ TL minimum since July 1, 2021. Limits apply to hook-and-line AND gig.
- **Oct–Nov:** Big females stage at inlets and jetties in Oct–Nov before heading offshore to spawn. Last good shot of the year.
- **Where (kid-friendliest first):** Myrtle Beach State Park Pier · Murrells Inlet MarshWalk / Morse Park Landing · Mount Pleasant Pier · Second Avenue Pier · Garden City Pier · Cherry Grove Pier
- **Bait:** Live finger mullet · Live mud minnows · Live menhaden
- **Lures:** Gulp! Swimming Mullet 3–4″ on 1/4 oz jighead · Bucktail tipped with Gulp
- **Rig it:**
  - *Saltwater rod:* Carolina rig: 1/2–1 oz egg sinker, bead, swivel, 18″ of 20 lb fluoro, 1/0–2/0 hook through the minnow's lips. Drag it SLOWLY along pilings/rocks; when you feel a thump, count to 10, then reel tight.
  - *Freshwater rod:* Same Carolina rig, lighter: 1/2 oz egg sinker, 15 lb fluoro, #1 hook. Great dock rig.
  - *Kids' Ugly Stik:* Mud minnow on a #2 hook under the pier; most kid flounder are under 16″, so measure every one.

### Sheepshead

*Also called: convict fish, sheephead*

- **ID:** 5–6 bold black vertical bars on silver-gray; human-like front teeth; very sharp back-fin spines.
- **Look-alikes:** Juvenile black drum also have bars but have chin barbels and no human teeth.
- **SC limits:** 14" min TL · 10/person/day · 30/boat
- **Oct–Nov:** Build up on jetties, pilings and bridges through late fall into winter.
- **Where (kid-friendliest first):** Murrells Inlet MarshWalk / Morse Park Landing · Mount Pleasant Pier · Garris Landing (Cape Romain NWR) · Huntington Beach SP: Murrells Inlet South Jetty
- **Bait:** Fiddler crabs · Barnacles / oysters scraped from pilings · Sand fleas
- **Lures:** Not a lure fish. Use bait.
- **Rig it:**
  - *Saltwater rod:* Short fluoro leader (6–8″, 20–30 lb), 1 oz egg sinker right above, strong #1–1/0 J-hook. Drop straight down tight to the structure; set at the slightest tick.
  - *Freshwater rod:* Too light for jetty rocks; use the saltwater rod.
  - *Kids' Ugly Stik:* Tough for kids (light bites). Let them scrape barnacles to chum.

### Black Drum

*Also called: drum, puppy drum (small)*

- **ID:** High arched back; many short chin barbels; gray-black (young have 4–5 vertical bars); makes a drumming sound.
- **Look-alikes:** Sheepshead: human teeth, no barbels. Red drum: tail spot, no barbels.
- **SC limits:** 14–27" TL · 5/person/day
- **Oct–Nov:** Steady at piers, bridges and inlets all fall.
- **Where (kid-friendliest first):** Garden City Pier · Cherry Grove Pier · Georgetown: East Bay Park / Winyah Bay · Huntington Beach SP: Murrells Inlet South Jetty
- **Bait:** Fresh shrimp (peeled or whole) · Clams · Cut blue crab
- **Lures:** Rarely: Fishbites on a bottom rig
- **Rig it:**
  - *Saltwater rod:* Fishfinder or 2-hook bottom rig, 2–3 oz sinker, 2/0 circle hook, shrimp on the bottom.
  - *Freshwater rod:* 2-hook bottom rig, 1–2 oz sinker, #1 hooks, shrimp.
  - *Kids' Ugly Stik:* 2-hook bottom rig with shrimp. Most small black drum come to kids this way.

### Whiting (Southern Kingfish)

*Also called: whiting, sea mullet, kingfish (small), king whiting*

- **ID:** Single short chin barbel; gray-silver; mouth underneath; long first back-fin spine.
- **Look-alikes:** Croaker has several barbels and a brassy color with wavy lines.
- **SC limits:** 50/person/day. 50/person/day COMBINED with spot + croaker (hook & line). No size limit.
- **Oct–Nov:** Strong fall fish in the surf troughs and around piers. The best kid fish on the coast.
- **Where (kid-friendliest first):** Surfside Pier · Myrtle Beach State Park Pier · Second Avenue Pier · Apache Pier · Springmaid Pier · Cherry Grove Pier
- **Bait:** Fresh shrimp (small pieces) · Sand fleas (mole crabs) · Bloodworms
- **Lures:** Fishbites (shrimp or sand flea flavor) on bottom rig
- **Rig it:**
  - *Saltwater rod:* 2-hook bottom (dropper) rig, #4–#2 hooks, 2–3 oz pyramid or bank sinker. Cast into the first trough.
  - *Freshwater rod:* Same 2-hook rig with 1–2 oz sinker; the freshwater rod works fine for whiting.
  - *Kids' Ugly Stik:* Pre-tied 2-hook rig, #6 hooks, 1–2 oz sinker, small pieces of shrimp. Short casts are fine; whiting are in the first trough.

### Spot

*Also called: spot, Lafayette*

- **ID:** Small, deep-bodied; one black spot just behind the gill; yellowish diagonal lines.
- **Look-alikes:** Pinfish: shoulder spot too, but blue/yellow stripes and spiny. Red drum: spot is on the TAIL.
- **SC limits:** 50/person/day. 50/person/day COMBINED with whiting + croaker. No size limit.
- **Oct–Nov:** October "spot run" along piers and in inlets (timing varies year to year).
- **Where (kid-friendliest first):** Myrtle Beach State Park Pier · Apache Pier
- **Bait:** Bloodworms · Small shrimp pieces
- **Lures:** Bloodworm Fishbites
- **Rig it:**
  - *Saltwater rod:* Double-dropper rig, #6 hooks, 1–2 oz sinker.
  - *Freshwater rod:* Double-dropper rig, #6 hooks, 1 oz sinker.
  - *Kids' Ugly Stik:* Perfect kid fish: double-dropper, #6 hooks, bloodworm Fishbites. Also great live bait for big reds/flounder.

### Atlantic Croaker

*Also called: croaker, hardhead*

- **ID:** Several tiny chin barbels; brassy-silver with wavy diagonal lines/spots; croaks when caught.
- **Look-alikes:** Whiting: one barbel, plain silver.
- **SC limits:** 50/person/day. 50/person/day COMBINED with whiting + spot. No size limit.
- **Oct–Nov:** Common around piers and inlets into November.
- **Where (kid-friendliest first):** Myrtle Beach State Park Pier · Second Avenue Pier · Apache Pier · Cherry Grove Pier · Pier 14
- **Bait:** Shrimp · Bloodworms · Squid strips
- **Lures:** Fishbites
- **Rig it:**
  - *Saltwater rod:* 2-hook bottom rig, #4 hooks, 2 oz sinker.
  - *Freshwater rod:* 2-hook bottom rig, #4–6 hooks, 1–2 oz sinker.
  - *Kids' Ugly Stik:* 2-hook bottom rig, #6 hooks, shrimp.

### Bluefish

*Also called: blues, snapper blue, chopper*

- **ID:** Blue-green back, silver sides, forked tail, rows of razor-sharp triangular teeth. Use pliers, not fingers.
- **Look-alikes:** Spanish mackerel has gold spots; jacks have a hard scute line near the tail.
- **SC limits:** 5/person/day. No size limit. 7/person on for-hire boats.
- **Oct–Nov:** Blitz the mullet schools along the beach and piers in October.
- **Where (kid-friendliest first):** Surfside Pier · Apache Pier · Springmaid Pier · Cherry Grove Pier · Folly Beach Pier · Pier 14
- **Bait:** Cut mullet · Cut menhaden · Live finger mullet
- **Lures:** Gotcha plug · Silver spoon (Hopkins, Clark) · Metal jig
- **Rig it:**
  - *Saltwater rod:* 6–12″ of light wire or 40 lb leader to a Gotcha plug; fast, jerky retrieve.
  - *Freshwater rod:* Metal spoon on a 30 lb leader; expect cut-offs without wire.
  - *Kids' Ugly Stik:* Cut mullet on a bottom rig with a short wire leader; adult unhooks.

### Spanish Mackerel

*Also called: spanish*

- **ID:** Gold/yellow oval spots on silver sides; front of first back fin is BLACK; lateral line slopes gently.
- **Look-alikes:** Young king mackerel: lateral line dips sharply under the 2nd back fin; no black on the 1st back fin.
- **SC limits:** 12" min FL · 15/person/day
- **Oct–Nov:** Leave as water cools through October; early-October pier mornings are the last shot.
- **Where (kid-friendliest first):** Surfside Pier · Springmaid Pier
- **Bait:** Live finger mullet · Glass minnows
- **Lures:** Gotcha plug · Clark spoon · Small silver metal jig
- **Rig it:**
  - *Saltwater rod:* Gotcha plug or 1 oz spoon on 30 lb fluoro or light wire; fast retrieve from the pier end at sunup.
  - *Freshwater rod:* Small spoon on 20–30 lb fluoro leader.
  - *Kids' Ugly Stik:* Spoon on a cast-and-reel. Fun but fast. An adult should rig it.

### King Mackerel

*Also called: king, kingfish, smoker*

- **ID:** Large, silver; lateral line drops sharply under the 2nd back fin; no black on the 1st back fin.
- **Look-alikes:** Spanish mackerel (see above).
- **SC limits:** 24" min FL · 3/person/day
- **Eating:** FDA lists king mackerel as a "choice to avoid" (high mercury), especially for kids and pregnant women.
- **Oct–Nov:** Sept–Oct pier-end kings when bait is thick (Cherry Grove, Apache, Springmaid king passes).
- **Where (kid-friendliest first):** Apache Pier · Springmaid Pier · Cherry Grove Pier · Folly Beach Pier
- **Bait:** Live menhaden · Live bluefish
- **Lures:** Pier king fishing is live bait
- **Rig it:**
  - *Saltwater rod:* Needs a dedicated king setup (anchor rod + trolley/stinger rig, 20–30 lb mono, wire stinger). Your saltwater spinning rod isn't built for it.

### Florida Pompano

*Also called: pompano*

- **ID:** Deep, flat silver body; yellow throat and belly; blunt head; no teeth.
- **Look-alikes:** Permit (rare here): deeper body, no yellow.
- **SC limits:** No size limit. No SC size or creel limit listed.
- **Oct–Nov:** Fall run along the beach in the surf, often with whiting.
- **Where (kid-friendliest first):** Pawleys Island (surf & creek) · Folly Beach Pier
- **Bait:** Sand fleas (#1) · Shrimp · Fishbites
- **Lures:** Small 1/4–1/2 oz pompano jig (yellow/pink)
- **Rig it:**
  - *Saltwater rod:* Pompano rig (2 hooks with floats/beads), #1–2 hooks, 2–3 oz pyramid sinker, sand fleas in the first trough.
  - *Freshwater rod:* Same pompano rig with 2 oz sinker.
  - *Kids' Ugly Stik:* Pompano rig with Fishbites; same as whiting fishing.

### Cobia

*Also called: ling, lemonfish*

- **ID:** Long dark-brown body, broad flat head, dark stripe down the side, short back-fin spines; looks shark-like.
- **Look-alikes:** Remora (sharksucker) has a suction disk on its head.
- **SC limits:** 36" min FL · 1/person/day · 6/boat. North of 32°31′N (the Grand Strand): 1/person, 6/boat. Circle-hook rule applies to natural bait 4/0+.
- **Oct–Nov:** Mostly a spring fish here; occasional pier-end fish.
- **Bait:** Live eels · Live menhaden
- **Lures:** Large bucktail jig
- **Rig it:**
  - *Saltwater rod:* Heavy gear. Not a target for this rod lineup.

### Pinfish

*Also called: pinfish, sailor's choice*

- **ID:** Small, spiny; dark shoulder spot; blue and yellow horizontal stripes.
- **Look-alikes:** Spot: shoulder spot but plain yellowish diagonal lines.
- **SC limits:** No size limit. No limit. Excellent live bait for reds and flounder.
- **Oct–Nov:** Everywhere around docks and pilings until water cools.
- **Bait:** Tiny pieces of shrimp
- **Lures:** Sabiki rig
- **Rig it:**
  - *Saltwater rod:* Sabiki or #8 hook with a pea of shrimp.
  - *Kids' Ugly Stik:* #8 hook, tiny shrimp piece. Endless bites.

### Hardhead Catfish (saltwater)

*Also called: sea catfish, gafftopsail*

- **ID:** Saltwater catfish: 4 chin + 2 corner barbels; VENOMOUS spines on back and side fins. Gafftopsail has long fin filaments.
- **Look-alikes:** Whiting / croaker have scales and no venomous spines.
- **SC limits:** Possession prohibited: release. Hardhead & gafftopsail: possession prohibited. Release immediately. Pin spines with a towel; a spine stab is very painful.
- **Oct–Nov:** Common bycatch on bottom rigs.

### Striped Bass

*Also called: striper, rockfish*

- **ID:** 7–8 unbroken dark horizontal stripes on silver; two separate back fins.
- **Look-alikes:** Hybrid: stripes broken/offset, deeper body. White perch: no stripes.
- **SC limits:** 10/person/day. Statewide freshwater: 10/day, no size limit. Special rules on Santee Cooper, Lake Murray, the Pee Dee-area rivers, and salt water.
  - *santee-cooper:* 23–25" TL · max 1 over 26" · 3/person/day · closed 06-16→09-30. Santee Cooper: Oct 1–Jun 15 only; 3/day, 23–25″ fish may be kept and ONE may be over 26″ (25–26″ must go back). Closed Jun 16–Sep 30.
  - *murray:* 21" min TL (10-01→05-31) · 5/person/day. Lake Murray: 5/day; 21″ min Oct 1–May 31; any length Jun 1–Sep 30.
  - *pee-dee-rivers:* 26" min TL · 3/person/day · closed 06-16→09-30. Pee Dee-area rivers: SOURCES CONFLICT (statewide 10/day vs 26″ min, 3/day, closed Jun 16–Sep 30). The stricter rule is applied here. Check the posted regs.
  - *sc-salt:* 26" min TL · 3/person/day · closed 06-16→09-30. Salt water: 26″ TL min, 3/day Oct 1–Jun 15; possession prohibited Jun 16–Sep 30. Circle-hook rule applies.
- **Oct–Nov:** Santee Cooper reopens Oct 1. Stripers school under birds and chase herring/shad as water cools. Mostly a boat fishery.
- **Where (kid-friendliest first):** Santee State Park (Lake Marion) · Georgetown: East Bay Park / Winyah Bay · Lake Murray: Saluda Dam North Rec Area pier · Lake Wateree State Park · Great Pee Dee River: US 76/301 Bridge Landing
- **Bait:** Live blueback herring · Live gizzard / threadfin shad · Cut herring
- **Lures:** Bucktail jig · Topwater walker when schooling · 4–5″ swimbait · Umbrella rig (boat)
- **Rig it:**
  - *Saltwater rod:* Live herring on a 3/0–5/0 circle hook, 30″ of 20 lb fluoro, 1 oz egg sinker (down-line) or free-lined.
  - *Freshwater rod:* Bucktail or swimbait to breaking fish; 10 lb braid / 15 lb fluoro leader.

## Freshwater

### Largemouth Bass

*Also called: bass, bigmouth, green trout*

- **ID:** Green with a dark, blotchy horizontal stripe; upper jaw extends PAST the back of the eye.
- **Look-alikes:** Spotted bass: jaw stops at the eye, rows of small spots below the lateral line, tooth patch on tongue.
- **SC limits:** 5/person/day. 5/day combined black bass. No statewide minimum.
  - *santee-cooper:* 14" min TL · 5/person/day. Santee Cooper lakes: 14″ minimum, 5/day.
  - *murray:* 14" min TL · 5/person/day. Lake Murray: 14″ minimum, 5/day.
  - *wateree:* 14" min TL · 5/person/day. Lake Wateree: 14″ minimum, 5/day.
  - *ashwood:* 3/person/day. Lake Ashwood (SCDNR state lake): 3 bass/day. Follow posted signs.
- **Oct–Nov:** Follow shad into creek arms and shallow flats; feed hard as water cools into the 60s°F. One of the best months of the year.
- **Where (kid-friendliest first):** Prestwood Lake (Lawton Park) · Little Pee Dee State Park · Lake Ashwood (SCDNR) · Carolina Sandhills NWR · Santee State Park (Lake Marion) · Cheraw State Park (Lake Juniper)
- **Bait:** Live shiners · Nightcrawlers (small bass)
- **Lures:** Buzzbait / walking topwater (dawn) · Lipless crankbait (shad color) · Spinnerbait · ChatterBait · 5″ stick worm (wacky or Texas)
- **Rig it:**
  - *Saltwater rod:* Works for heavier cover (spinnerbait, ChatterBait) if spooled with 20 lb braid.
  - *Freshwater rod:* Texas-rigged 5″ stick worm: 3/0 EWG hook, 1/8 oz bullet weight (or weightless). Or a 1/2 oz lipless crank burned over grass.
  - *Kids' Ugly Stik:* Live shiner or nightcrawler under a bobber near cover. Kids catch plenty of bass this way.

### Bluegill

*Also called: bream, brim, copperhead*

- **ID:** All-black "ear flap"; dark blotch at the back of the soft back fin; faint vertical bars; yellow-orange breast.
- **Look-alikes:** Redear: orange-red edge on ear flap, no back-fin blotch. Redbreast: long skinny ear flap, river fish.
- **SC limits:** 30/person/day. 30/day bream aggregate (bluegill, redear, warmouth, redbreast), no size limit.
  - *ashwood:* 15/person/day. Lake Ashwood: sources say 15–20 bream; 15 applied (stricter).
- **Oct–Nov:** Leave the shallow beds for brush piles and docks in 6–12 ft.
- **Where (kid-friendliest first):** Lynches River County Park · Prestwood Lake (Lawton Park) · Lee State Park · Little Pee Dee State Park · Lake Ashwood (SCDNR) · Carolina Sandhills NWR
- **Bait:** Red wigglers · Crickets · Pieces of nightcrawler
- **Lures:** 1/32 oz tube or curly-tail jig · Beetle Spin · Small inline spinner
- **Rig it:**
  - *Freshwater rod:* 1/32 oz jig under a small slip float, or #8 hook + split shot + worm.
  - *Kids' Ugly Stik:* THE kid fish. Clip-on bobber 2–3 ft above a #8 long-shank hook, small split shot, piece of worm. Long-shank hooks are easier to unhook.

### Redear Sunfish

*Also called: shellcracker, bream*

- **ID:** Black ear flap with a red/orange edge; no dark blotch on the back fin; often bigger than bluegill.
- **Look-alikes:** Bluegill (all-black flap + back-fin blotch).
- **SC limits:** 30/person/day. 30/day bream aggregate.
  - *ashwood:* 15/person/day
- **Oct–Nov:** Bottom feeders on snails; hold deeper than bluegill in fall.
- **Where (kid-friendliest first):** Prestwood Lake (Lawton Park) · Lake Ashwood (SCDNR)
- **Bait:** Red wigglers on the bottom · Crickets
- **Lures:** Small jig fished on the bottom
- **Rig it:**
  - *Freshwater rod:* Bottom rig: 1/4 oz sinker, 12″ leader, #8 hook, worm.
  - *Kids' Ugly Stik:* Bobber set deep (bait near the bottom), worm.

### Redbreast Sunfish

*Also called: redbreast, robin, river bream*

- **ID:** LONG narrow black ear flap; males have a bright orange-red belly; lives in rivers (Lynches, Little Pee Dee, Black).
- **Look-alikes:** Bluegill (short ear flap, lakes).
- **SC limits:** 30/person/day · (≤15 of this species). 30/day bream aggregate, but no more than 15 redbreast.
- **Oct–Nov:** Hold in eddies behind logs and along shaded banks as rivers drop.
- **Where (kid-friendliest first):** Lynches River County Park · Lee State Park · Black River State Park (The Meadows)
- **Bait:** Crickets · Red wigglers
- **Lures:** Beetle Spin · Small Rooster Tail
- **Rig it:**
  - *Freshwater rod:* Beetle Spin cast past a log and reeled slowly back.
  - *Kids' Ugly Stik:* Cricket on a #8 hook under a small bobber along the bank.

### Warmouth

*Also called: goggle-eye, bream*

- **ID:** Big mouth for a sunfish; red eye; dark lines radiating back from the eye; mottled brown.
- **Look-alikes:** Rock bass (not common here), small largemouth.
- **SC limits:** 30/person/day. 30/day bream aggregate.
- **Oct–Nov:** Around stumps and cypress knees in swamps and rivers.
- **Bait:** Worms · Small minnows · Crickets
- **Lures:** Small jig · Beetle Spin
- **Rig it:**
  - *Freshwater rod:* #6 hook, split shot, worm next to wood.
  - *Kids' Ugly Stik:* Bobber + worm tight to stumps.

### Crappie

*Also called: speckled perch, specks, papermouth, slab*

- **ID:** Silver with black speckles (black crappie) or faint vertical bars (white crappie); big paper-thin mouth; large back and anal fins.
- **Look-alikes:** Bluegill: small mouth, ear flap.
- **SC limits:** 8" min TL · 20/person/day. 8″ minimum, 20/day statewide (incl. Santee Cooper).
- **Oct–Nov:** Move from mid-depth brush piles to creek channels and suspend near shad. October minnow bite on Santee Cooper brush.
- **Where (kid-friendliest first):** Santee State Park (Lake Marion) · Lake Murray: Saluda Dam North Rec Area pier · Lake Wateree State Park · Lake Moultrie: Fred L. Day Pier · Santee NWR (Lake Marion)
- **Bait:** Live crappie minnows
- **Lures:** 1/16–1/8 oz jig with 2″ tube or curly tail · Small hair jig
- **Rig it:**
  - *Freshwater rod:* Slip float set to just above the brush, #4 light-wire gold hook, live minnow hooked through the lips.
  - *Kids' Ugly Stik:* Fixed bobber, #4 gold hook, minnow. Lift gently; crappie mouths tear easily.

### Channel Catfish

*Also called: channel cat, fiddler (small)*

- **ID:** Deeply forked tail; ROUNDED anal fin (24–29 rays); small dark spots on younger fish.
- **Look-alikes:** Blue catfish: straight-edged anal fin (30–36 rays), no spots.
- **SC limits:** No size limit. No statewide creel listed in the 2026–27 guide (verify on posted signs).
  - *ashwood:* 3/person/day. Lake Ashwood: sources say 3–5 catfish; 3 applied (stricter).
- **Oct–Nov:** SCDNR: "October could be a very good month for catfish." Fish move deeper as water cools.
- **Where (kid-friendliest first):** Lynches River County Park · Lee State Park · Little Pee Dee State Park · Lake Ashwood (SCDNR) · Carolina Sandhills NWR · Cheraw State Park (Lake Juniper)
- **Bait:** Nightcrawlers · Chicken liver · Cut shad · Stink bait (punch bait)
- **Lures:** Not a lure fish
- **Rig it:**
  - *Saltwater rod:* Same slip-sinker rig for big cats.
  - *Freshwater rod:* Carolina (slip-sinker) rig: 1/2–1 oz egg sinker, swivel, 18″ of 15 lb line, 2/0 circle hook. Rod in a holder; let it load up.
  - *Kids' Ugly Stik:* Slip-sinker rig with a #2 circle hook + nightcrawler; kid sits by the rod.

### Blue Catfish

*Also called: blue cat, blue*

- **ID:** Slate blue-gray, no spots; anal fin has a STRAIGHT edge like a barber comb (30–36 rays). Grows huge.
- **Look-alikes:** Channel catfish (rounded anal fin, spots).
- **SC limits:** max 2 over 32" · 150/person/day. New May 15, 2026 (Act 120): 150/day in most waters. Max 2 over 32″ in Santee Cooper, upper Pee Dee, Congaree & Wateree rivers.
  - *santee-cooper:* max 2 over 32" · 25/person/day. Santee Cooper: 25/day, max 2 over 32″.
  - *pee-dee-upper:* max 2 over 32" · 25/person/day. Pee Dee River NC line → US 301 bridge: 25/day, max 2 over 32″. (Below the bridge: 150/day.)
- **Eating:** SCDES advisories cover blue catfish on several Pee Dee-area rivers. Check the spot's advisory before keeping any.
- **Oct–Nov:** Drift or anchor cut bait on channel ledges; big fish start moving to deeper water for winter.
- **Where (kid-friendliest first):** Santee State Park (Lake Marion) · Lake Moultrie: Fred L. Day Pier · Great Pee Dee River: US 76/301 Bridge Landing
- **Bait:** Cut gizzard shad · Cut white perch · Cut herring
- **Lures:** Not a lure fish
- **Rig it:**
  - *Saltwater rod:* Santee-Cooper drift rig: 1–2 oz bell sinker on a 3-way, 24″ of 40 lb leader, 5/0–7/0 circle hook, chunk of cut shad.
  - *Freshwater rod:* Slip-sinker rig with 3/0 circle hook. Big blues will test this rod.

### Flathead Catfish

*Also called: flathead, mudcat, yellow cat*

- **ID:** Wide, flat head; LOWER jaw sticks out past the upper; square/rounded tail; mottled yellow-brown.
- **Look-alikes:** Channel/blue cats have forked tails.
- **SC limits:** No size limit. No statewide creel listed in the 2026–27 guide (verify on posted signs).
- **Oct–Nov:** Feeds at night near deep wood in rivers (Pee Dee, Lynches).
- **Where (kid-friendliest first):** Great Pee Dee River: US 76/301 Bridge Landing
- **Bait:** Live bream (legal; counts toward your bream limit) · Live shad
- **Lures:** Not a lure fish
- **Rig it:**
  - *Saltwater rod:* Live bream on a 5/0–7/0 circle hook, 2–3 oz slip sinker, 40 lb leader, near deep logjams at night.

### White Perch

*Also called: white perch*

- **ID:** Silvery, deep body, NO stripes (or very faint); usually under 12″. Big in Santee Cooper.
- **Look-alikes:** Striped/white bass have stripes.
- **SC limits:** No size limit. No SC limit found. Verify.
- **Oct–Nov:** Big schools on Santee Cooper. Fast action and great cut bait for blue cats.
- **Where (kid-friendliest first):** Santee State Park (Lake Marion)
- **Bait:** Small minnows · Worms
- **Lures:** 1/8 oz jigging spoon · Small jig
- **Rig it:**
  - *Freshwater rod:* Jigging spoon straight down on schools seen on sonar/under birds.
  - *Kids' Ugly Stik:* Minnow on a #4 hook under a bobber.

### Bowfin

*Also called: mudfish, blackfish, grinnel, choupique*

- **ID:** Long back fin running most of the body; rounded tail; males have a black eyespot at the tail base; mouth full of teeth.
- **Look-alikes:** Snakehead (invasive, report it!) has a long anal fin too and a pelvic fin near the head.
- **SC limits:** No size limit. No SC limit found. Verify.
- **Eating:** Many Pee Dee-area waters carry DO-NOT-EAT advisories for bowfin. Release.
- **Oct–Nov:** Swamps, backwaters and river oxbows; aggressive biters.
- **Where (kid-friendliest first):** Lynches River County Park · Black River State Park (The Meadows) · Great Pee Dee River: US 76/301 Bridge Landing
- **Bait:** Cut bait · Live minnows
- **Lures:** Spinnerbait · Swimbait
- **Rig it:**
  - *Freshwater rod:* Spinnerbait along cypress edges. Use pliers; they bite.

### Chain Pickerel

*Also called: jackfish, jack, pike*

- **ID:** Long, thin body; duck-bill snout; dark chain-link pattern on green-gold sides; very sharp teeth.
- **Look-alikes:** Redfin pickerel (smaller, bars instead of chains).
- **SC limits:** 30/person/day. 30/day, no size limit.
- **Oct–Nov:** Bites better as water cools; ambushes from weed and cypress edges.
- **Bait:** Live minnows
- **Lures:** Inline spinner · Spoon · Jerkbait
- **Rig it:**
  - *Freshwater rod:* Inline spinner; add 12″ of 20 lb fluoro so teeth don't cut you off.
  - *Kids' Ugly Stik:* Minnow under a bobber near weeds.

## The family's rods

### Saltwater rod

- **Assumed:** 7′ medium / medium-heavy spinning, 3000–4000 size reel
- **Spool:** 20 lb braid main line → 24–30″ of 20–30 lb fluorocarbon leader (double uni or FG knot)
- Rinse rod + reel with fresh water after EVERY trip; back the drag off before storing.
- Braid has no stretch: keep drag at ~1/3 of line strength and let circle hooks set themselves (reel, don't jerk).
- Pier: bring a drop net or long-handle pier net. You can't lift a 5 lb fish 20 ft on 20 lb line.

### Freshwater rod

- **Assumed:** 6′6″–7′ medium spinning, 2500 size reel
- **Spool:** 10 lb braid → 6 ft of 8–10 lb fluorocarbon leader, or straight 8 lb monofilament (simplest)
- Straight mono is more forgiving for live-bait and bobber fishing; braid + leader is better for lures and casting distance.
- Re-tie after every big fish or every ~hour of fishing around wood and rocks.

### Kids' Ugly Stik

- **Assumed:** Ugly Stik GX2 youth combo (spincast or spinning, 4′6″–5′6″)
- **Spool:** 8 lb monofilament for freshwater; 10–12 lb mono for pier/surf
- Pre-tie rigs at home (bobber rigs + 2-hook bottom rigs) in a labeled tray; re-rigging tangles eats the whole trip.
- Size 6–8 hooks for bream; size 4–6 for whiting/spot/croaker. Small hooks = more bites for kids.
- Not for bull reds, kings, big cats, or stripers: hand those fights to an adult rod.
- Spincast reels: hold the button, swing, release at the 10 o'clock position.
